blocks.text: of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and for as long as Hadhrat Ali (RA) remained in Madinah (as Khalifah before moving the capital to Kufa). Thereafter, he kept the post for a further five years until Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) became the Khalifah in the year 40 A.H. Even after this, he remained instated in the position until he passed away in the year 45 A.H." [^1]

Hadhrat Ataa bin Yasaar reports that both Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) used to call for Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) (to consult with) and would also consult with the veterans of the Battle of Badr. Until the day he passed away, Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) used to issue Fataawaa during the time of Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA). [^2]

Hadhrat Ziyaad bin Meenaa narrates that amongst those Sahabah (RA) who issued Fataawaa and narrated Ahadeeth in Madinah were Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA), Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah Amr bin Al Aas (RA), Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA), Hadhrat Raafi bin Khudayj (RA), Hadhrat Salamah bin Akwa (RA), Hadhrat Abu Waaqid Laythi (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Buhaynah (RA). This they continued doing from the time Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) passed away until their deaths. Amongst them, the ones who issued the bulk of the Fataawaa were Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA), Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) and Hadhrat Jaabir bin Abdullaah (RA). [^3]

Hadhrat Qaasim relates, "During the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and until the time she passed away (may Allaah shower his mercy on her), (my aunt) Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) used to issue Fataawaa by herself. I used to stay with her and she showed extreme affection towards me." [^4]
The Statement of Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) concerning the Vast Knowledge of the Sahabah (RA)
Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) said, "Rasulullaah ﷺ left us with so much knowledge that even when a bird fluttered its wings in the sky, it would remind us of something he had taught us." [^5]
